summary: [¶] f) The observations of the Commission in para 125 of the impugned order, clarify that the data on GCV furnished by NTPC is erroneous and based on assumptions and hence cannot be considered for the computation of IoWC. In the impugned order, the Commission has deviated from the methodology as specified by it in the tariff order dated 3.3.2017 to arrive at the ‘as received GCV’ of coal. While in the tariff order, the Commission directed the determination of ‘as received GCV’ of coal, based on the adjustment formula, in the impugned order, it has adopted the so-called ‘as received GCV’ data furnished by NTPC, which were never submitted during the proceedings for tariff determination nor was shared with the Review Petitioner with the bills or furnished in the truing-up Petition or reflected in Form-15 of the Regulations. [¶] - e) Even otherwise, this Commission _vide_ the impugned order observed that the GCV of coal on an ‘as received' basis, which was submitted by NTPC for the months of January 2014 to March 2014, was taken into consideration, after a prudence check, while passing the impugned order. T his Commission, after doing a prudence check of the GCV value of coal on an ‘as received' basis, which was submitted by NTPC, considered the appropriate value of GCV of coal for the computation of IoWC. Therefore, there is no error apparent, and hence the present Review Petition is not maintainable. [¶] - j) This Commission vide its order dated 3.3.2017 in Petition No. 280/GT/2014 in respect of this generating station for the period 2014-19 had taken into consideration the provisional GCV value of coal on “as billed basis”. This means that the aforesaid was an ad hoc interim arrangement taken by this Commission. In light of the aforesaid submissions, the impugned order passed by this Commission holds good in law. [¶] - m) During the pendency of the said tariff petition, this Commission directed NTPC to submit the GCV of coal on an ‘as received’ basis in accordance with Regulation 28(2) of the 2014 Tariff Regulations. However, this Commission vide its order dated 25.1.2016 in Petition No. 283/GT/2014, inter-alia, held that the most appropriate method for computation of Energy Charge Rate is on the basis of the measurement of GCV of coal on ‘as received’ basis, which is in line with the 2014 Tariff Regulations. [para 11] 11. We have examined the matter. It is noticed that against the Commission’s order dated 21.4.2022 in Petition No.362/GT/2020 (truing up of tariff of Kahlagaon STPS, Stage-II for the period 2014-19), the Review Petitioner has filed Appeal No.258/2022 before APTEL on the issue viz., computation of IoWC on the basis of ‘as billed’ GCV of coal for the period of January 2014, to March 2014. The present Review Petition filed by the Review Petitioner is against the impugned order dated 11.1.2024 in respect of truing-up of the tariff of Farakka STPS, Stage-III for the period 2014-19, being considered in this order. It is therefore evident that the appeal filed by GRIDCO before APTEL is in respect of the Commission’s order for a generating station (Kahalgaon STPS), which is different from the Commission’s order in respect of a generating station [¶] existence only on 25.1.2016 (after the Commission’s order in Petition No. 283/GT/2014), NTPC has clarified that, hence, in Form 15, it was mentioned that it did not have the infrastructure for measuring the figures of ‘as received GCV’ for the aforesaid months.
